title: ‘Harry Potter’ HBO Series Casts Dobby, Ginny Weasley and Tom Riddle for ‘Chamber of Secrets’ Season 2
description:
Hogwarts just got a little bit bigger.

	HBO has announced a few new castings for Season 2 of its upcoming “Harry Potter” series.

	Dobby will be pl
body:
Hogwarts just got a little bit bigger.

	HBO has announced a few new castings for Season 2 of its upcoming “Harry Potter” series.

	Dobby will be played by Lenny Rush, Ginny Weasley will be played by Bonnie Hill and Tom Riddle will be portrayed by Billy Barratt. Hill will replace Gracie Cochrane, who portrays Ginny Weasley in Season 1 but exited the role “due to unforeseen circumstances.”


	The first season of the “Harry Potter” TV show has wrapped and will premiere on HBO on Dec. 25. The second season, which will be based on the second book of J.K. Rowling’s beloved fantasy series, is currently in pre-production at Leavesden Studios outside London.
	

	For the few who haven’t read the books or seen the movies, HBO’s “Harry Potter” logline reads: “There is nothing special about Harry Potter — or so his Aunt Petunia tells him. But when a mysterious letter of admission to Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry arrives, it opens the door to a hidden world of magic, friendship and adventure. Yet behind Hogwarts’ enchanted walls lie dark secrets. Harry must find the courage to prove himself against the darkest wizard of all.”

	Dominic McLaughlin will lead the small screen adaptation as The Boy Who Lived, while Arabella Stanton is playing Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout is Ron Weasley. Rounding out the cast are John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape, Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid, Rory Wilmot as Neville Longbottom and Lox Pratt as Draco Malfoy, plus dozens of other actors playing familiar characters.
	

	The “Harry Potter” show is based on Rowling’s books and is written and executive produced by Francesca Gardiner. Mark Mylod will executive produce and direct multiple episodes of the series for HBO in association with Brontë Film and TV and Warner Bros. Television. The series is executive produced by Rowling, Neil Blair and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV, as well as David Heyman of Heyday Films.

schema.headline: ‘Harry Potter’ HBO Series Casts Dobby, Ginny Weasley and Tom Riddle for ‘Chamber of Secrets’ Season 2

title: Donald Trump Sounds Off on Maria Bartiromo’s Shock Exit From Fox News: Her ‘Many’ Fans ‘Will Not Be Happy’
description: President Donald Trump reacted to Fox News’ surprise announcement Thursday that it has parted ways with Maria Bartiromo, who had been an anchor on F
body:
President Donald Trump reacted to Fox News’ surprise announcement Thursday that it has parted ways with Maria Bartiromo, who had been an anchor on Fox News and Fox Business Network for more than 12 years.

	Fox News did not provide a reason for its dismissal of Bartiromo, a former prominent CNBC anchor who joined Fox Business in 2014. She last appeared Fox News on Aug. 9.

	In recent years, Bartiromo, nicknamed “The Money Honey” during her two-decade tenure at CNBC, has become increasingly enamored of Trump and receptive to various MAGA conspiracy theories.
	

	“I can’t believe Maria Bartiromo is no longer going to have her great show(s) on FoxNews/Business,” Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social account Thursday evening. “Three different shows, always number one. Maria is a total professional, and a true warrior. Her fans, of which there are many, will not be happy. God bless you, Maria! President DONALD J. TRUMP”

	Citing a source familiar with the situation, Variety reported that Fox News believes Bartiromo shared with the White House a directive that the network’s bosses issued to executive producers at Fox Business cautioning staffers against supporting outlandish claims made by Trump. Bartiromo had wanted to pursue a story about Trump’s claims in a July 16 speech, in which he alleged recent U.S. elections had been “rigged and stolen” and claimed China had illegally accessed millions of voter files to try to manipulate American elections in 2018 and 2020, per media industry newsletter Status.

	Divulging confidential company information to an outside party would likely be seen as a violation of terms of employment. A Fox News spokesperson Thursday called Bartiromo’s departure “a business decision.”
	

	Bartiromo was the first Fox anchor to promote false claims about the 2020 presidential election. She was among Fox News staffers including Sean Hannity and Jeanine Pirro who were named in a $1.6 billion defamation lawsuit filed by voting technology company Dominion Voting against Fox News in 2021. Fox ultimately agreed to settle the matter for $787.5 million. 

	The Dominion lawsuit alleged Bartiromo had allowed false claims about the 2020 presidential election to air on the network as part of a bid to keep pro-Trump viewers from abandoning Fox News.

	Bartiromo has not commented on her exit from Fox as of this writing. Bartiromo has retained Hollywood attorney Bryan Freedman, who has worked with Megyn Kelly and others who have had conflicts with media employers, Variety reported.

	Brian Steinberg contributed to this story.

schema.headline: Donald Trump Sounds Off on Maria Bartiromo’s Shock Exit From Fox News: Her ‘Many’ Fans ‘Will Not Be Happy’

title: Ann Hui, Carlo Chatrian to Head Pingyao’s Fei Mu, Rossellini Juries
description: The Pingyao International Film Festival has named Hong Kong director Ann Hui and Italian critic and programmer Carlo Chatrian as jury presidents of
body:
The Pingyao International Film Festival has named Hong Kong director Ann Hui and Italian critic and programmer Carlo Chatrian as jury presidents of the Fei Mu Awards and the Roberto Rossellini Awards, respectively, ahead of the festival’s 10th edition, running Sept. 24–30, in Pingyao, China.

	The Fei Mu Awards, recognized by Fei Mu’s family, aim to carry on Fei Mu’s aesthetic legacy, support up-and-coming filmmakers from Chinese-speaking regions and encourage the development of Chinese-language films. Recipients are selected from among the Chinese-language feature films in the Hidden Dragons section.
	

	The Roberto Rossellini Awards were established at the festival by Fondazione Roberto Rossellini and honor the director’s humanist legacy, celebrating outstanding films and the young directors who make them while championing cinema as an art form. Winners are selected from films by emerging international directors in the Crouching Tigers section.


	Hui, a film director born in Anshan, China, moved to Hong Kong at age five and was educated there. She holds a master’s degree from the University of Hong Kong, where she studied English and Comparative Literature, before training at the London Film School. She entered the film industry as an assistant to director King Hu in 1975, then joined Television Broadcasts Limited and RTHK’s television unit. Her 1979 directorial debut, “The Secret,” established her as a defining figure of the Hong Kong New Wave. “The Spooky Bunch” (1980) and her Vietnam Trilogy – “The Boy from Vietnam” (1978), part of the “Below the Lion Rock” series, “The Story of Woo Viet” (1981) and “Boat People” (1982) – solidified her early reputation as a filmmaker to watch.
	

	Hui has directed over 20 films to date. Her major works include “Summer Snow,” “Ordinary Heroes,” “The Way We Are,” “A Simple Life,” “The Golden Era” and “Our Time Will Come,” along with literary adaptations such as “Love in a Fallen City,” “Eighteen Springs,” “Love After Love,” “The Book and the Sword” and “The Postmodern Life of My Aunt.” Her films have earned six Hong Kong Film Awards for best film and six for best director, placing her among the most decorated filmmakers in that award’s history. The Asian Film Awards gave her its Lifetime Achievement Award in 2011, and the Venice Film Festival honored her with the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at its 77th edition in 2020. She has also served as president of the Hong Kong Film Directors’ Guild and holds the vice chair role at the Hong Kong International Film Festival Society.

	Chatrian, a journalist, author and programmer, was born in Torino. He has contributed film criticism to numerous newspapers and magazines over the years. He led the Locarno Film Festival as artistic director from 2013–2018, then held the same post at the Berlinale from 2020–2024, and has served on festival juries at Sundance, Toronto, Tokyo, Morelia and Hong Kong. He now directs the National Museum of Cinema in Torino and belongs to both the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and, separately, the Academy of Italian Cinema.

	The festival said the rest of the jury lineup would be confirmed at a later date.

schema.headline: Ann Hui, Carlo Chatrian to Head Pingyao’s Fei Mu, Rossellini Juries

title: Global Content Industry Leaders Gather to Discuss ‘Multilateralism for the Moving Image’ at France’s Lumiere Summit
description: Hollywood heavyweights and top players in content and exhibition from around the world will gather in Saint-Paul-de-Vence on Sept. 7 for the landmar
body:
Hollywood heavyweights and top players in content and exhibition from around the world will gather in Saint-Paul-de-Vence on Sept. 7 for the landmark Lumiere Summit that aims to explore the future of film at a time of profound change that is transforming media and entertainment.

	The daylong event, to be held at the renowned art foundation complex Fondation Maeght, has been organized by France’s CNC, the state unit that oversees policy for film, TV, video games and digital content. The Lumiere Summit is co-chaired by French President Emmanuel Macron Lee Jae Myung, president of South Korea. It’s designed to generate dialogue to address the many vexing issues that have upended the business models of film and other forms as content, as well as the wide swings in consumer tastes and media consumption habits that are challenging the traditional industry in the U.S. and beyond.
	

	Gaëtan Bruel, president of CNC, cited Macron’s dictum that the situation calls for nothing less than “multilateralism for the moving image” to preserve the art and the commerce of movies and other forms of entertainment.


	“The response must address the entire ecosystem: image literacy, access to works, film heritage, the future of art-house cinemas, piracy, sustainability or the transformations driven by technology and artificial intelligence. But it also needs a method, what President Macron calls ‘multilateralism for the moving image’: bringing sectors and continents together to forge a shared vision and turn it into action,” Bruel said. “We are advancing this ambition alongside South Korea, another great film nation, one that has combined a vibrant domestic cinema with a confident global audiovisual ambition. Above all, we are doing so with 220 participants from five continents, representing 65 countries and every part of the industry.”
	

	LISTEN: Netflix, Disney+ and Amazon Fight in France Over Streaming Quotas and Theatrical Windowing Rules

	The summit offers a rare opportunity for senior executives, exhibitors, producers, distributors, talent representatives, financiers and other key constituencies to gather for deep conversations about where market forces are driving consumers and commerce.

	“President Macron wanted to put cinema and the moving image where they belong: at the heart of the defining debates of our time,” Bruel said. “Because what is at stake extends far beyond the screen industries. Our entire image-based civilization is at a turning point. How we create, produce, distribute, watch and pass on stories is changing profoundly, with consequences for individuals and societies alike.”

	Summit organizers are emphasizing the urgency of the world community to gather to address budding opportunities and structural challenges that need to be addressed through policy, contracts and trade agreements.

	The CNC has recruited Variety to serve as the Lumiere Summit’s official media partner. Variety will offer extensive coverage of the summit’s sessions, key speakers and in-depth analysis of the substance of what is discussed throughout the week.

	Notable attendees from the U.S. making the trek to Saint-Paul-de-Vence are Netflix’s Ted Sarandos, Disney’s Dana Walden and Alan Bergman, NBCUniversal’s Donna Langley, HBO’s Casey Bloys, Sony Pictures’ Tom Rothman, Paramount Skydance’s Andy Gordon, Regal Cinemas’ Eduardo Acuna, Sony Pictures Classics co-chief Michael Barker; Lynette Howell Taylor, producer and Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences president; CAA chief Bryan Lourd and Directors Guild of America leader Russ Hollander, as well as boldface names such as George Clooney and producer-director Anthony Russo.

	The event has also drawn a who’s who of industry leaders from across Europe, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East and Africa, including Rodolphe Belmer, CEO of TF1, EbonyLife Group’s Mo Adubu, Mubi’s Efe Çakarel, Mediawan’s Pierre-Antoine Capton, CJ ENM’s Miky Lee, Canal+’s Maxime Saade and Studiocanal’s Anna Marsh, Vue’s Tim Richards and Cannes Film Festival chief Thierry Frémaux.

	The guest list was carefully curated to encourage debate and the dissection of difficult issues ranging from the transformative effects of AI to combating piracy to assuring the veracity of artistic vision on the screen.
	

	“The summit is deliberately small, but it is not closed,” Bruel said. “The full program is public, every session will be recorded and made available online, and we are especially proud to partner with Variety, one of the world’s most trusted and influential voices on cinema and entertainment, to ensure that the conversations sparked in Saint-Paul-de-Vence resonate throughout the global screen community.”

	(Pictured: Netflix’s Ted Sarandos, HBO’s Casey Bloys, NBCUniversal’s Donna Langley, Sony Pictures’ Tom Rothman and Disney’s Dana Walden)

schema.headline: Global Content Industry Leaders Gather to Discuss ‘Multilateralism for the Moving Image’ at France’s Lumiere Summit

title: ‘A Place to Heal’ Review: Cédric Kahn’s Rawly Sensitive Film Chronicles the Daily Tumult of an Adolescent Psychiatric Ward
description: “A Place to Heal” is an unduly sentimental English-language title title for French writer-director Cédric Kahn’s new feature, which goes internation
body:
“A Place to Heal” is an unduly sentimental English-language title title for French writer-director Cédric Kahn’s new feature, which goes internationally by the more prosaic (if outwardly cryptic) “15/18” — referring, simply, to the age bracket of the teenage residents in the psychiatric ward where most of the drama is confined. It’s a place to be treated, certainly, but for many of these nervy, damaged adolescents, healing is hard to come by, and the film does little to soften or idealize their plight. Following the 2023 double-shot of his taut legal drama “The Goldman Case” and playful industry satire “Making Of,” Kahn’s latest finds him working in the unfussily humane mode of 2017’s “The Prayer,” keeping the filmmaking simple while counting on the vibrant spontaneity of his mostly inexperienced young ensemble for fireworks.   
	

	The result recalls Laurent Cantet’s comparably documentary-styled, youth-focused “The Class,” or the more rigorous work of Belgium’s Dardenne brothers — at least until a final act that briefly and rather poignantly makes a break for more romanticized fiction. That unexpected swerve may divide audiences, though it’s a welcome rogue instinct in a film that, while greatly affecting, isn’t altogether unfamiliar. A competition berth at Venice — Kahn’s first at one of the European majors since 2018 — will aid the profile of a low-key work with raw emotional impact; the film should secure specialist theatrical distribution outside France, though it would fit well on arthouse streaming platforms too.


	It begins on a note of clattering, disruptive angst, much of it courtesy of actress Malou Khebizi — one of the few pros in the young cast, having previously brought that same brash, feral energy to Agathe Riedinger’s 2024 Cannes competition entry “Wild Diamond.” She plays 17-year-old Lucia, a recurring patient at this closed ward in a public hospital in an unspecified French town, introduced being readmitted for another stint, but not without a fight. 
	

	Lashing out in fury as her phone and lighters are confiscated — she knows the drill, but is still loath to submit to it — she’s back after the latest in a series of suicide attempts, all of which, she says, were “because of boys.” The staff greet her with jaded, none-too-welcoming recognition: In this job, reunions are never happy occasions. She has one friend to welcome her back, however: Eloïse (Zoé Monpart), a slight, frail longtime resident perhaps more quietly serious than Lucia about wanting to die. “Why don’t they respect my wishes?” she asks, as her suicidal ideations are once again brushed off by tough-loving nurse Carole (Sophie Guillemin, wonderful), who’s trained not to indulge such sentiments. 

	Not that callousness is the default approach on this ward: Led by experienced head psychiatrist Etienne (played with a creased air of authority by Kahn himself), the staff are characterized with as much care and detail as their charges, as we see the daily toll that the kids’ anguish takes on them in turn. New intern Jules (Antoine De Foucauld) frequently acts as the audience’s proxy in this intense, sometimes frightening hothouse of rage and vulnerability: After he weathers a physical assault at his first patient assessment, he’s not sure he can hack it, and it’s hard to blame him.

	Co-written with Kahina Le Querrec — previously a costumer on “The Prayer,” where she and Kahn met — the loosely structured script was developed through extensive first-hand observation in equivalent psychiatric wards, though all characters and events have been fictionalized. For its first half, especially, “A Place to Heal” threads together casually sequenced vignettes that collectively capture  the rough and tumble of everybody life on the ward, alternating between garrulous group scenes — a mealtime argument over the background music that devolves into an aggressive food fight — and more intimate dialogues between patients and supervisors: In one heartbreaking exchange, junior psychiatrist Paola (Jennifer Decker), whose approach is rather less formal than Etienne’s, gently but firmly counters the insistence of shy domestic abuse survivor Yasmine (Ahleme Sahraoui) that her family’s intent was to protect her rather than hurt her.

	With the arrival of volatile new patient Enzo (an electrifying Kenji Peyran), who swiftly forms romantic attachments to both Lucia and Eloïse, the film takes on a more streamlined narrative shape, toward a propulsive finale that surprisingly abandons the ensemble dynamic to focus on one character’s cathartic change in routine — one that leads at least to the precipice of recovery. 
	

	It’s a sharp shift from the jittery, chattering communal rhythm that characterizes most of the film. The tight, interrogative framing and keenly responsive movement of DP Patrick Ghiringhelli’s cinematography — often using multiple cameras for maximal docu-style candor in any given scenes — gives way, at least briefly, to lung-filling wide shots. You don’t notice quite how claustrophobic the ward is until you’re outside of it: Kahn’s tender but incisive film makes it both a necessary sanctuary and an airless purgatory, safe from the outside world but not from inner demons.

schema.headline: ‘A Place to Heal’ Review: Cédric Kahn’s Rawly Sensitive Film Chronicles the Daily Tumult of an Adolescent Psychiatric Ward

title: Rising Pop Badass Adéla Arrives in a Big Way With ‘Prima’: Album Review
description: Being eliminated from the “Dream Academy” reality-TV series that produced Katseye might be the best thing that ever happened to 22-year-old Slovakia
body:
Being eliminated from the “Dream Academy” reality-TV series that produced Katseye might be the best thing that ever happened to 22-year-old Slovakian native Adéla Jergová: After a summer of lighting up festival stages from Lollapalooza to Reading, the arrival of “Prima” makes it more obvious than ever that a group couldn’t contain her.

	While her debut EP, last year’s “The Provocateur,” was hard-edged in sound and subject matter, her full-length bow tempers the toughness with a softer, dare we say more feminine touch, not only in the sound but the songwriting: The beats are hard but there are lighter pop hooks, and the combination makes for a sound that’s both more memorable and more unusual.
	

	The melodic strength of the album isn’t surprising: Executive-produced by 100 Gecs’ musical wizard-turned-pop savant Dylan Brady and Blake Slatkin (who’s co-crafted hits for everyone from Sam Smith and Sienna Spiro to Charli xcx and Lil Nas X), the bulk of the album was written by them and Adéla with fellow top-shelf hitmakers Julia Michaels and Billy Walsh. This A-team brought their A-game, but what’s most striking is the variety of styles the album covers: There are flashes of Ariana Grande, Charli xcx, Lady Gaga, a waft of “College Dropout”-era Kanye West in the sped-up R&B loop on “Nicole Kidman” and a chopped-and-screwed hook on the closing “Ain’t in LA,” one of the year’s best singles.


	But there’s never any question whose show this is: Adéla’s fiery personality swaggers all over the album, moving from confrontational badass to breathy seductress to heartbroken girlfriend, and her lyrics can be offhandedly hilarious: “Nobody wants dirty shoes/ nobody wants dad issues”; “Lately I’m lackin’/ A sense of reciprocity in your passion”; “Playing Nirvana, ride you in your Honda/ I like how you look at me like I’m the next Madonna.”
	

	With hooks and attitude for days, “Prima” feels poised to be one of the breakthrough albums of the year. We’d say “a star is born” but it’s obvious Adéla knows she already is one.

schema.headline: Rising Pop Badass Adéla Arrives in a Big Way With ‘Prima’: Album Review

title: Lea Salonga on ‘Miss Saigon,’ ‘Aladdin’ and Supporting Her Trans Son Amid Anti-Trans Rhetoric: ‘It Makes Me Intensely Afraid and Not Just for My Child’
description:
Tony winner Lea Salonga admits she never really thought about getting a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

	“Most of my work is in musical theater
body:
Tony winner Lea Salonga admits she never really thought about getting a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

	“Most of my work is in musical theater,” says Salonga, who earned international recognition for originating the role of Kim in “Miss Saigon” in 1989. “So even though musical theater does reach Los Angeles and Hollywood, it’s not something that I thought would actually happen. It’s not like the kind of Hollywood career that, say, somebody like Bette Davis or Katharine Hepburn or any of those icons of the screen or television have had. This is something that I did not foresee.”
	

	But on Friday, Salonga will become the 2,855th recipient of a Hollywood Walk of Fame star and makes history as the first Filipina to receive the honor.


	While she is known as a star of the stage, Salonga has had major roles on screen, too. She was the singing voice for Princess Jasmine in “Aladdin” as well as Fa Mulan in “Mulan” and “Mulan 2.” Later this month, Salonga, who made her singing debut when she was just seven years old in her native Manila, appears in “Forgotten Island,” DreamWorks Animation’s Philippines-set fantasy adventure about childhood friends who get trapped in the mystical world of Nakali.

	“It centers on my culture,” Salonga tells me over a Zoom video call earlier this week. “It centers Philippine myth and folklore. We get to share our mythological creatures with the bigger world. I don’t think it’s something that I ever thought I would have seen.”

	Salonga was 17 years old when she landed “Miss Saigon” in the original West End production of the show before transferring to Broadway. She auditioned with a performance of “On My Own” from “Les Misérables” followed by “The Greatest Love of All.” After several call backs, including a trip to London, “I was told, ‘You’re in the show, but we don’t know what role we’re going to give you,’” Salonga recalled. “Never mind that at this point the only songs I was learning were the ones sung by Kim. But I was like, ‘Whatever.’ I was pre-med in college. I had a life. So if you decide you’re going to put me in the ensemble, I’ll just be like, ‘Thank you, but no thank you.’”
	

	Salonga’s work as Kim earned her a Laurence Olivier Award and in 1991, she became the first Asian actress to win a Tony Award and the second-youngest actress to win for best performance by a leading actress in a musical.

	She was still in “Miss Saigon” when she was cast in “Aladdin” in the early 90s. “Stage management and the powers that be were so kind in saying, ‘You’re we’re going to give you the night off because we want you to sound great for that recording session,’ which I really appreciated,” Salonga said. “Given that ‘Little Mermaid’ and ‘Beauty and the Beast’ had come out, I think they had a feeling that this was going to be huge.”

	In the decades since, Salonga has starred in several Broadway musicals and released numerous albums. She frequently appears on the Manila stage.

	She has also become a fierce LGBTQ+ ally and activist. Her actor and singer son Nic Chien came out as trans in 2025. “We felt that it was important for all of this to be made very public,” Salonga says. “There have been young people that have slid into his DMs and have said, ‘Thank you for what you are doing. Thank you for what you and your mom are doing because I think this is also who I am, and it’s giving me strength and inspiration.’

	“My son was reading one of those letters aloud in our kitchen in Manila,” she continues. “We were both doing a show together at the time and I think he was realizing how much of an impact he was making just by being who he is.”



	

									Getty Images for Tony Awards Pro
	



	As for politicians who are using anti-trans rhetoric and pushing for anti-trans legislation, Salonga says, “It makes me angry and upset. It makes me intensely afraid, and not just for my own child, but for a lot of other young people who just want to live, who just want to exist and make a living for themselves and fall in love.”

	But she adds, “They’re basically trying to say, ‘Look over there,’ because chances are if somebody’s telling you to look somewhere else, you start looking into their backyards. Something is happening, and they’re trying to distract. If they’re trying to, you know, take our attention away from themselves, something’s up.”

schema.headline: Lea Salonga on ‘Miss Saigon,’ ‘Aladdin’ and Supporting Her Trans Son Amid Anti-Trans Rhetoric: ‘It Makes Me Intensely Afraid and Not Just for My Child’

title: TikTok Creator Skyelar Chase Signs With Innovative Artists Entertainment
description: Digital creator Skyelar Chase, who specializes in luxury lifestyle content and has more than 1.7 million followers on TikTok, has signed with Innova
body:
Digital creator Skyelar Chase, who specializes in luxury lifestyle content and has more than 1.7 million followers on TikTok, has signed with Innovative Artists Entertainment for representation in all areas.

	The agency will work with Chase to strategically expand her growing presence across the fashion, beauty, travel and lifestyle spaces. She did not previously have agency representation. 


	The Korean American creator has “become a go-to source for all things luxury and is quickly becoming a leading tastemaker,” according to Innovative Artists. Based in New York City, Chase is currently enrolled as a student at Columbia University studying film.
	

	Chase joins the roster of talent repped by Innovative Artists, which includes Amanda Seyfried, Paul Anthony Kelly, Grace Van Dien, Carlos Manuel Vesga, Christian Convery and LaChanze. Last year, the company sold a minority stake to L.A.-based private equity firm Coral Tree Partners. 


	Across TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, Chase has built an audience of over 2.5 million followers. According to Innovative Artists, her “consistently polished aesthetic, personal style and aspirational yet relatable content includes taking her global audience behind the scenes at major industry events like global fashion weeks and high fashion house engagements.” 

	Chase has been tapped by publications like InStyle and Who What Wear for exclusive coverage about her insider access at fashion week shows. In addition, she has partnered with luxury brands such as Miu Miu, Fendi, Tiffany & Co., Prada, Valentino Beauty, Dior Beauty, Dolce & Gabbana Beauty and L’Oréal Paris.
	

	In June, she was in Padua, Italy, to attend an event hosted by Valentino:

title: Jeff Zucker on How He Ended Up Playing Himself in A24’s ‘Primetime’: ‘Jacob Elordi Wasn’t Available’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: As an actor, Jeff Zucker makes for a good TV executive. So when he was approached by “Primetime” filmmaker Lance Oppenheim to play “Jeff Zucker” in
body:
As an actor, Jeff Zucker makes for a good TV executive. So when he was approached by “Primetime” filmmaker Lance Oppenheim to play “Jeff Zucker” in the new A24 movie, the real Jeff Zucker couldn’t resist.

	“Primetime” stars Robert Pattinson as former “Dateline NBC” reporter Chris Hansen, whose segment on the newsmagazine executed sting operations designed to catch child predators. Soon, “To Catch a Predator” was a phenomenon — but it also led to controversy, which the film tackles. 
	

	In the film, then-NBCUniversal TV Group CEO Jeff Zucker is seen congratulating Hansen on his success. “I don’t really like your show,” Zucker says in the cameo, as seen in the “Primetime” trailer. “But America loves it. So I need to move you, ‘To Catch a Predator’ — 9 p.m. Primetime!”


	Yep, he actually says the movie’s title — almost guaranteeing that he wouldn’t end up on the cutting room floor. And he didn’t. Variety recently caught up with Zucker — who will be attending the “Primetime” premiere at the Venice Film Festival this weekend — to get the details on how he wound up playing Jeff Zucker in a major motion picture.
	
		What are you doing, Jeff? How did this happen? Who reached out?	

	I did not know anything about the project, and it turns out that Lance Oppenheim, the director, went to college with my son. He was a year ahead of Andrew at Harvard, and they were friendly there. They were talking about this film that Lance was directing, and he said, “Hey, I’m doing this film, and who should I get to play your father?” And my son Andrew said, “Well, why don’t you ask my father to do it?” Lance said, “Would he do it?” And Andrew said, “I don’t know. Ask him!” So Andrew connected us, and Lance explained what he was doing. I said, “OK, I’ll do it,” just as a lark.
	
	
		Did you read the script first? 	

	He sent me the pages of my scene, and he was clear with me that obviously this was, as they say, “inspired by true events.” The scene in which I play myself never happened. It’s obviously a fictional scene. He sent me those pages and they were fine, they portrayed me as a ratings-driven network entertainment executive — pretty far from the truth, right?



	

					Jeff Zucker in “Primetime”
	


	
		Sounds more like they nailed it.	

	In other words, exactly. So, they sent me the pages, I was fine with them. And about a year ago, I went down to New Orleans, and shot the scene with Robert Pattinson for a full day.
	
		You said you agreed to do this as a lark, but what was going through your head when you said yes?	

	Listen, I think I try not to take myself too seriously. It was a fun ask, and I haven’t been given that many opportunities to do a scene in a film opposite Robert Pattinson, so I figured, why not? Let’s have fun. And that’s what it was. I don’t know if you recall, back in the day when I was running NBC Entertainment, I did the show “Fat Actress.” Remember that, with Kirstie Alley?
	
		I remember the show, but I don’t remember you doing that.	

	I did “Fat Actress” with Kirstie Alley. In fact, I was in a bathtub with Kirstie Alley, and I did “My Name Is Earl,” which I think you remember as well. So I acted in those shows. In “Fat Actress,” I played myself as well. So I had done a couple TV appearances. I had never done a film, and I thought, why not? Let’s have fun. And that’s really how it all came about. And here we are!
	
		So you already had your SAG card then. Had you kept it up? Had you been paying for it?	

	That’s a really good question. The answer is yes. I had my SAG card from way back when, and I’ve paid my annual dues for probably 25 or 26 years now.
	
		So you’re still voting for SAG Awards every year?	

	Well, I didn’t say that, but I pay my annual dues!
	
		“Primetime” takes place in 2006, so you’re playing yourself 20 years younger. Let’s talk about that. Did they age you down?	

	That’s funny. That’s a good point. I don’t think we ever really thought about how old the character was at the time. As you probably know, they reconstructed my NBC Entertainment office, and I have to say they did a pretty good job. They did it with pictures from that time, and they dressed me in a suit from that era. A big boxy, broad-shoulder tan suit. I think they also saw that from pictures. It was kind of funny to walk back in time like that. I don’t think we ever really thought about the fact that I was playing somebody 20 years younger because I don’t think that anybody ever really cared what the age of that character was per se.
	
	
		Perhaps it’s a compliment that maybe you just haven’t aged.	

	There you go. I think we’ll go with that.



	

					Jeff Zucker in “Primetime”
	


	
		From the few bits that I’ve seen in the trailer, I was most impressed with the scheduling board. 	

	That is the amazing thing. That scheduling board was really true to form. They really nailed it, and they definitely got that right. As I said, the scene never happened in real life, but the scheduling board is absolutely real.
	
		Down to all the competitive network schedules!	

	The names of the shows at the time. Exactly.
	
		Even the obscure ones. I’ve got to hand it to them. It seems like they really wanted to get this right.	

	Yeah, they took that from pictures of the time, which is kind of funny. I guess I kind of remember taking photos in front of that board, probably for Variety, but who knows!



	

					Weekly Variety, Jan. 16, 2006 issue
									Variety
	


	
		The movie takes place in 2006, and there is no shortage of stories that we were writing about you back then.	

	I’m sure. And by the way, I wasn’t running NBC Entertainment per se in 2006. It reported to me. As you recall, I ran NBC Entertainment from 2001 to 2005, and then I came back to New York to run the entire television group. So entertainment still reported to me, but I wasn’t actually running day-to day entertainment at the time.
	
		They’re taking some liberties, like you mentioned.	

	That’s why I said, the scene never happened, but you know, “inspired by true events” is certainly fair enough.
	
		Did you give any notes? What were your notes to the production in terms of, “I would have done it this way.”	

	That’s a good question. They were very receptive. They allowed me to improvise a little bit at the scheduling board. We tried it a couple different ways. It was just a fun experience. Obviously, a serious topic. I don’t want to diminish in any way the importance of the topic here, and this is obviously a serious topic within the movie. 
	
		Chris Hansen has been very vocal so far, even though he hasn’t seen the film yet, but he seems to have some real concerns about it. What do you make of that? What do you think he’s ultimately going to think when he sees it?	

	Look, I think that Chris will appreciate the way Robert Pattinson plays him, and I think he’ll know that this is not meant to be a factual documentation of what happened at that time, but certainly is representative of that era and the show. I think Chris will recognize that he was doing a lot of important work back then with these investigations.
	
	
		So what’s the reaction that you’ve gotten from colleagues, past and present, when they discover you did this?	

	I have a new moniker now. Everybody calls me “Primetime,” right? I actually was shocked at the number of people that saw the trailer and reached out. It’s been incredibly amusing to see the reaction. It’s been fun, and I think people are getting a real kick out of it. Honestly, I’m in the film for, I don’t know if that scene lasts 75 or 90 seconds. But because of the key line where I’m giving the title of the film, I’m in the trailer. So it generated a lot of attention that I hadn’t expected.
	
		Since you’re going to Venice, will you be campaigning for the film?	

	I will not. I will be a guest and enjoying the experience. I’ve never been to the Venice Film Festival. I didn’t ever really expect to go, and so when this came up, I said, how can I say no?
	
		Meanwhile, don’t forget the other acting that you did through the years. There were quite a few taped bits you did for the NBC upfronts.	

	That is absolutely true. Yes, we can’t forget “Fear Factor.”
	
		I’m thinking of the time that you went shirtless in a bit with the “Friends” cast as the show’s “Ugly Naked Guy.”	

	That’s right, I remember that one too!
	
		Listen, that one is seared in my brain.	

	I’m sorry about that.
	
		So if you hadn’t agreed to play yourself, who would you have recommended to producers to play “Jeff Zucker”?	

	Oh, that is a really good question. I assume Jacob Elordi probably wasn’t available, right?
	
		Yeah, I think it would have been either him or you. There were really no other options. So what’s your next role after this?	

	Don’t worry. I’m not standing by my phone waiting for the next the next offer. I have it all in perspective.
	
		I mean, eventually there’ll be an “Apprentice” movie, right?	

	By the way, I’m kind of surprised there hasn’t been, right?
	
		Maybe it’s too close to the bone, too soon, given everything going on.	

	I don’t know. I’m not going to comment on that one!

	This interview has been edited and condensed.

schema.headline: Jeff Zucker on How He Ended Up Playing Himself in A24’s ‘Primetime’: ‘Jacob Elordi Wasn’t Available’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Adria Arjona Details ‘Superman’ Sequel Training Amid Wonder Woman Rumors: 2 Hours of Weightlifting, 6 Rounds of Boxing and More
description: Sadie Sink had to dodge questions for months over whether or not she was playing Jean Grey in the lead-up to “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” and now it
body:
Sadie Sink had to dodge questions for months over whether or not she was playing Jean Grey in the lead-up to “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” and now it seems like DC star Adria Arjona may have to do the same for the “Superman” sequel, “Man of Tomorrow.” 

	Details about her role have remained shrouded in mystery, but DC fans are speculating that Arjona will debut as Wonder Woman in the rebooted superhero universe. While promoting her new action movie “Onslaught,” Arjona explained her workout regime in a video with Women’s Health, and it sounds like the sort of rigorous training an Amazonian superhero would undergo.
	



	“I’ve been boxing for years now. I think it’s something that allows me to get out of my head. You have to be so present at boxing because you can get punched. Boxing has made me so confident. Nothing makes you more confident than punching something, to be hitting it hard and hearing that pad. You’re like, ‘Hell yeah, I’m I’m powerful,'” she says in the video. “I think boxing has taught me that I can learn things quick. So it makes me feel really confident when learning lines or learning certain combos or even doing stunts. I feel more confident because throughout the years I’ve been able to learn these combos. They stay with me. When I show up to set and have to do a stunt choreography, I just feel strong.”


	Arjona was originally reported to be playing the villain Maxima, an alien queen who’s been a villain and love interest for Superman in the comics, in “Man of Tomorrow” next year. But then, rumors began to swirl that Maxima was really a decoy and she would actually be playing Wonder Woman, who was previously brought to life by Gal Gadot in the DCEU. Arjona explained her “Man of Tomorrow” training, but didn’t name the character she’s playing.
	

	“I wake up. I do cardio for about 45 minutes,” she explained. “Then I do weightlifting for about two hours. Then after the workout, I’ll have a bite to eat. We’ll box for six rounds and then I eat again. And then I eat and I eat and I go to sleep. It’s a job. I’m really enjoying it. I’m enjoying the transformation, but it’s it’s hard work. I’ve never felt stronger, but it’s hard. The excitement of playing the woman I’m playing gives me everything I need to wake up. Physically, it’s exhausting, but it’s all for the greater good.”

	DC fans may have to wait a bit longer to find out who Arjona is playing; “Man of Tomorrow” releases in theaters on July 9.

            Amber Eggers -- who starred on the show "Love After Lockup" -- has died after being hospitalized in Georgia, TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Her mom, Monica Eggers, tells TMZ ... Amber died Thursday night at a hospital in Atlanta after she was admitted several days earlier because she wasn't feeling well. Monica said doctors couldn't keep Amber's heart beating any longer, and her daughter ultimately died from acute liver failure.
      
    
            You may recall ... Amber appeared on Season 2 of We TV's popular reality series, "Love After Lockup," which aired in 2019. Amber was dating Vincent Gonzalez while she was behind bars, and they even got engaged ... but their relationship ended after she got out.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Amber and her former cellmate Michelle “Puppy” Deaton also made cameos on other "Love After Lockup" seasons, as well as the spin-off series, "Life After Lockup."
      
    
            Amber was 41.

title: Ex-Kentucky Governor Reportedly Arrested on Set of Christmas Film
description:
Ex-Kentucky Governor Matt Bevin
                          Arrested For Contempt Of Court
body:
Ex-Kentucky Governor Matt Bevin
                          Arrested For Contempt Of Court
                          While Shooting Xmas Movie
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 4, 2026
                            5:55 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Former Kentucky Governor Matt Bevin found himself behind bars Thursday for contempt of court -- and he was reportedly arrested on the set of a Christmas film.
      
    
            Police busted Bevin while he was playing an extra on the set of the holiday movie production in Bourbon County, KY, according to Louisville Public Media.
      
    
            The ex-governor was then transported to the Louisville Metro Department of Corrections, where he was booked for "contempt of court libel/slander resistance to order." Bevin also posed for his not-too-happy mug shot.
      

            His legal troubles reportedly stemmed from failing to turn over his financial records to a judge in his ongoing divorce and child support case. The judge reportedly found Bevin in contempt of court and issued an arrest warrant ... but LPM reports that wasn't the only one he faced this year.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The first was for not appearing at a court hearing in May, which Bevin reportedly blamed on a boulder that struck his vacation home in Maine ... but he paid a fine, and the judge rescinded the warrant.
      
    
            Then the judge dinged Bevin with a second arrest warrant after he failed to cough up his financial records. This time, Bevin was unable to pay the fine, so the warrant stayed active ... and now he's under arrest.
      
    
            LPM reports both Matt's ex-wife Glenna and their son appeared in person at the July hearing, but a party tried joining the courtroom via Zoom multiple times but was ultimately dropped from the call after alleghedly failing to identify themselves.
      
    
            Bevin was the 62nd Governor of Kentucky, serving from 2015 to 2019.

title: Former New York Jets QB Mark Sanchez Intends To Plead Guilty in Assault Case
description:
Former NFL Star Mark Sanchez
                          Intends To Plead Guilty Days Before Jury T
body:
Former NFL Star Mark Sanchez
                          Intends To Plead Guilty Days Before Jury Trial Begins
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              
                September 3, 2026
                
                            2:25 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 3, 2026
                                4:09 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Mark Sanchez has agreed to plead guilty in connection to the stabbing incident that took place in Indianapolis last year ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to court documents ... the former New York Jets star came to an agreement with prosecutors just 5 days before his criminal trial was set to begin -- asking the judge to set aside the trial start date and "set this matter for a guilty plea and sentencing hearing."
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Sanchez's legal advisor, Nick Sanchez Jr., said, “This is a positive development. We are finalizing an agreement with the prosecutor’s office that provides a path toward resolving the state’s case. We’re also encouraged by the constructive conversations taking place regarding the related civil matter. There is real momentum toward bringing this entire chapter to a close."
      

            Matt Goliko -- the attorney for Sanchez's alleged victim Perry Tole -- also tells us, "We are pleased with the constructive and professional conversations we’ve had with Mr. Sanchez’s team. Our discussions have been productive, and we’re on a positive path toward an agreement that will allow the parties to move forward. Mr. Tole appreciates the progress we have achieved and looks forward to an amicable resolution.”
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Sanchez was hospitalized in Indianapolis last year after an altercation with Tole -- during which Tole told cops Sanchez became very aggressive toward him, causing him to fear for his life and use a weapon in self-defense.
      
    
            Prosecutors charged Sanchez with felony battery involving serious bodily injury shortly after cops arrested him in a hospital bed.
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Fox Sports fired Sanchez from his job as a broadcaster weeks after the incident. Sanchez was in Indianapolis to work as a commentator on a game.

title: Mistrial in Lindsay Clancy Case
body:
Lindsay Clancy
                          Mistrial!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 4, 2026
                            8:18 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
        
                    
                  
      
    
            Wow -- Reddington just told the judge he wanted to immediately go to the Massachusetts Supreme Court to reverse what he called "this travesty." He asked the judge not to dismiss the jury until the Supreme Court ruled. The judge gave Reddington 1 hour to go to the Supreme Court.  This is high tension.
      
    
            The jury in Lindsay Clancy’s murder case was unable to reach a verdict, and the judge just declared a mistrial.
      
    
            They deliberated for 38 hours ... 2 hours after the judge said the lone holdout could remain on the jury.
      
    
            The jury has sent the judge a note ... saying it was with a heavy heart that the jury could not reach a unanimous verdict.
      
    
            The judge said after sending the jury back twice, he was required by law to declare a mistrial.
      
    
            Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, argued the judge had discretion to make the jury press on, but the judge rejected the argument.
